Preprint (arXiv), formatted for ACM Trans. Softw. Eng. Methodol. (template placeholders Vol. 1, No. 1; acceptance not stated)

Shenzhen Technology University (H. Chen, Z. Yang, J. Li, M. Li, Y. Chen); Shenzhen University (H. Lin); Shandong University (L. Zhang); Huazhong University of Science and Technology (A. Li); Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences (D. Zan); all China

Proposes an approach (EnvPilot, experience-augmented environment-setup agent with Trajectory-Derived Memory and Context-aware Retrieval), evaluated against baselines with ablations; secondary: proposes an evaluation method (AES-Bench benchmark, 112 instances, plus LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation)

EnvPilot (no version), built on an adapted SWE-Agent framework. Baselines: SWE-Agent (adapted for environment setup), RepoLaunch (SWE-bench-Live), ExecutionAgent, Repo2Run (adapted, Python only), Installamatic (non-agentic), Bash-based Agent (EnvBench, adapted); no versions given

Trajectory-Derived Memory (TDM): 667 JSON entries <problem, solution, action> distilled from 781 SWE-Agent trajectories by DeepSeek-R1-0528, stored in Milvus; structured codebase profile (JSON schema: language/version, package manager, build tools, test framework, system dependencies) extracted from README, config and CI files; 3-5 hypothetical queries per task. Outputs: command sequence, trajectory, test log. Not specifications

Learn-Retrieve-Act-Evaluate cycle: (1) Learn: distil trajectories into TDM; (2) Retrieve: codebase-profile extraction, hypothetical query generation, multi-query cosine retrieval + Reciprocal Rank Fusion (top k = 10); (3) Act: ReAct-style setup in Ubuntu 22.04 container (max 50 turns), run tests; (4) Evaluate: LLM-as-a-Judge (DeepSeek-V3) on test lifecycle; new experiences added to TDM (TDM frozen during evaluation)
None during runs. One-time: 3-5 expert-annotated seed examples for the distillation prompt; manual audit of a random 5% sample (~34) of TDM entries
Full workflow except continuous learning (TDM frozen at the initial 667 entries during evaluation); ablations remove or replace TDM, retrieval and memory format
Not classifiable (experience memory / retrieval-augmented agent; no specification); authors use no SDD terms
Existing code bases: environment setup and test execution for open-source GitHub repositories at fixed commits

AES-Bench: 112 instances from 99 repositories (>=1000 stars), 9 languages, 12-13 per language; average files per repo by language 1,013 (JavaScript) to 7,255 (Java). ExecutionAgent-Bench: 50 tasks. Max 50 interaction turns per task
Software environment setup for open-source projects in C, C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, PHP, Python, Rust, TypeScript (server-side and library projects; no monorepos, mobile or embedded)
N/A (autonomous agent, no participants); human experts labelled 460 trajectories (profile not stated)
Average API calls (interactions) per task; average tokens per task (K); average dollar cost per task (based on token usage). No wall-clock time

Benchmarks: AES-Bench (112, disjoint from TDM repositories) and ExecutionAgent-Bench (50). Configurations: EnvPilot vs 6 baselines x 2 models (DeepSeek-V3-0324, GPT-4o-mini) + 5 ablations + retrieval size k = 0-20. Baseline: adapted SWE-Agent (EnvPilot's base framework; = w/o TDM). Held constant: same container image, hardware, resource limits, shared tools, temperature 0.0, top-p 1.0, max 50 turns; official baseline prompts where possible. Acceptance: project's own test suite run to completion, judged by LLM judge. Repetitions: 3 runs (median) for EnvPilot and SWE-Agent, 1 for other baselines; 3 trials for stability. Human intervention: none during runs

EnvPilot best on success in both benchmarks and both models: AES-Bench DeepSeek-V3 75.00% vs SWE-Agent 62.50% (+12.5 pts) for +$0.005 per task; vs RepoLaunch +19.6 pts; GPT-4o-mini 46.43% vs RepoLaunch 40.18%; ExecutionAgent-Bench 72.00% vs 56.00%. Ablation: full system +8.04 pts over best ablation; removing TDM -12.5 pts; fewest API calls (28) but slightly more tokens (220K vs 200K). Stability: +11.91 pts mean (19.14% relative). Exceptions: C/C++ best without TDM (68.00% vs 60.00%); JS/TS best with unstructured memory; RepoLaunch stronger on Java/C/C++ with GPT-4o-mini. No statistical significance test

Distinguished EnvPilot from baselines and ablations (ablations B-E tied at 66.96%). Repeatable: only EnvPilot and SWE-Agent repeated 3 times (SD up to 4.09 pts); LLM judge agrees with humans (accuracy 98.04%, F1 98.34%). Limitations stated: binary success coarse; possible bugs in baseline reimplementations; pre-training leakage; single Linux distribution/hardware; repeated trials expensive

Open-source repos with public registries only (industrial private mirrors, network limits not covered); one Linux distribution and hardware profile; no very large monorepos, data-intensive, hardware-dependent, mobile or embedded projects; binary success metric ignores partial setups; residual failures (toolchain/runtime 60%, native dependencies 16%, platform constraints 16%, repo-config mismatch 8%); over-thinking on trivial tasks; retrieved experience misapplied in C/C++. Future: larger repositories, richer execution feedback, collaboration with developers, release of trajectories and evaluation scripts
